definition: the weak focus I hold at bedtime so that its failing tells me I have crossed

settled:
Sleep is the slip out of focus mode into diffuse mode. Any focus at all holds me at the surface: thinking about a problem, reading, listening properly to something.

I cannot drop into diffuse mode directly, so I ride a weak focus and let it give out under me. A count, a page of a book, or the small steering I get over the pictures at the edge of sleep. Three anchors, one move.

The breakdown is not a failure. It is the reading. I am not focusing myself to sleep. I am using focus as a gauge for the exact moment focus is no longer needed.

When it goes I stop. Put the book down, drop the count, and let the diffuse mode I have just detected take me the rest of the way.

Everywhere else in my regulation the focal grip is the tool and I hold it, because watch-and-feel mindfulness has nothing in me to rest on. Here it is the gauge, and the whole point is to feel it slip.

title: The Anchor I Let Give Out
